title: gcom-backed resolveHost must map 404 to empty result, not error
answers: How should a stack-lookup function report 'not found' vs 'error'?
Why does the single-tenant fallback silently skip some stacks?
What should resolveHost return when the stack ID doesn't exist in gcom?
single tenant fallback returns wrong host / doesn't fall back
body: newGComURLResolver in pkg/router/st_fallback.go returns ("", nil) when gcom answers 404 for GET {gcomBaseURL}/instances/{stackID} — this is treated as 'no fallback host', not an error. Any other non-200 status or a JSON decode failure returns a non-nil error instead. ProvideCloudRoutesLoaderFactory in pkg/router/cloud_router.go wires this function in as the `resolveHost` callback for newSingleTenantFallback, and the fallback cache/lookup path distinguishes empty-string-no-error (stack unknown) from an error (transient failure). Any future resolveHost implementation (or change to this one) must preserve that 404-is-not-an-error contract or the fallback cache will start caching/propagating spurious errors for legitimately missing stacks.
applies: pkg/router/st_fallback.go resolveHost implementations and callers of ProvideCloudRoutesLoaderFactory
